name: The example
expr: (lambda cap, items, t: 'the answer must be a list with one amount per item' if not isinstance(t, (list, tuple)) or len(t) != len(items) else 'every amount must be between 0 and the weight of its item' if any(not (-1e-9 <= x <= w + 1e-9) for x, (w, v) in zip(t, items)) else 'the amounts weigh more than the bag holds' if sum(t) > cap + 1e-6 else sum(x * v / w for x, (w, v) in zip(t, items)))(args[0], args[1], how_much(args[0], list(args[1])))
why: Worth 16.75: all 5 kg of (5, 10), 1 kg of (4, 7) and all 2 kg of (2, 5), so [5, 1, 0, 2]. Each test reports the value of your plan, or what is wrong with it. Taking the most valuable or the lightest item first is worth less.

show: a bag of 2,500,000 kg and 200,000 items weighing about 5,000,000 kg in all
why: About half the items go in. Sort the positions once, O(n log n). Picking the best remaining item with a full scan each time is O(n) per item, about 10 billion steps here.
